legacy: computeReview in index.html (07_engine.js) on the rows of parseBaseRows, run through tools/engine-host.js with the page's own upload path: totalCMV, totalInv, totalGL, invMissing, assetAllocation.rows, liqPie, allocByClient and allocByDistributor
new: app/src/engine/review.ts computeReview on app/src/ingest/load-base.ts: totals, assets, liquidity, byClient and byDistributor
notes: Every difference between the two outputs on the synthetic fixtures (the variants of the synthetic book and of tools/make-sample-base.js's book, both families, and the overview variants except hostile) must match exactly one entry, and every entry must be used, under TZ=Asia/Kolkata and TZ=UTC.

Both sides are projected into one shape before comparing (tests/parity/aggregation-compare.ts): Crore amounts, percentages as percent numbers, labels as strings, a missing value as null. Rows are matched by label and their order is compared on its own. The new matrices' not-given columns are paired with the legacy column labelled with the dash.

Diff kinds: total, asset-row, product-row, row-order, liquidity, matrix-col, matrix-cell, column-label. Keys name the row: the asset class; the class and product; the liquidity label; the level and column; the level, row and column of a cell.

An entry's key is an exact key, a list of keys, or a regular expression written between slashes. Classes follow 08-regression-test-plan.md section 5.4: correction (a known defect fixed, KI or OD named), improvement (a requirement changes the output), regression (a defect of the new code; must be empty for a merge).

The hostile variant is not run through the legacy engine: an Asset Name such as constructor or __proto__ reaches the legacy aMap (a plain object) and makes computeReview throw or write to Object.prototype.

entries.description: Two market values written as text that is not a number ("1.25 Cr", "12abc") are INVALID SOURCE DATA, so those holdings are excluded from every total and listed (BF-21). The legacy parseFloat read 1.25 and 12 Crore off the front of the text and counted both, which inflated the total market value, every percentage, the Equity and Mutual Funds rows, the client and distributor columns and their order.

The invested value written as "1.25 Cr" is INVALID SOURCE DATA and stays missing (BF-22), so that holding counts as one without an invested value and its class shows no invested value; and the two holdings excluded for an invalid market value (AG-01) take their invested values out of the totals. The legacy read 1.25 Crore off the text and summed the excluded holdings' invested values too. Gain follows as CMV minus invested over the holdings that have one.

The legacy read no holding from a file whose header is in row 6, or whose holdings follow a notes sheet, so it had no totals, rows, liquidity or matrices; the new reader finds the holdings (BF-11, BF-12) and the review shows them.

A holding with a blank Asset Name is Unknown, a class row of its own placed last, never Equity (BF-14). The legacy counted it in Equity, so its Equity row, product rows and matrix cells held it; in the total-like files that is the whole Grand Total row read as a holding (KI-142, a High result in the new app).
"Fixed Income" and "Debt Funds" count as Debt (BF-15, BF-16), so the Debt row holds them. The legacy kept each label as an allocation row of its own.
The spaced form "REITs / InvITs" reads as the class REITs/InvITs (BF-20), so it joins that row. The legacy made it a second row beside REITs/InvITs.

entries.description: An Asset Name the reader does not recognise ("Gold") is Unknown (BF-19, pending the owner's confirmation), so its holding is in the Unknown row. The legacy made "Gold" an allocation row of its own.

entries.description: "  EQUITY  " reads as Equity (BF-26, pending the owner's confirmation), so its holding is in the Equity row. The legacy kept "EQUITY" as an allocation row of its own beside Equity (KI-145).

The Equity row, its products and its matrix cells lose the holding with a blank Asset Name, which is Unknown (BF-14), and gain the one labelled "  EQUITY  " (BF-26, pending the owner). The legacy counted the blank one in Equity and kept "EQUITY" apart.

The Unknown row holds the holding with a blank Asset Name (BF-14) and the one labelled "Gold" (BF-19, pending the owner). The legacy had no such row: the blank one was Equity and "Gold" a row of its own.

The client and distributor matrices list the classes in the one asset order of every allocation: Equity, Debt, Hybrid, Commodity, REITs/InvITs, Unknown (the previous owner's order of 4 Jun). The legacy level matrices used Equity, Hybrid, Debt, Commodity (07_engine.js:2056), unlike its own Asset Allocation.

Holdings without a Client Name (or Distributor Name) go to a column labelled "Client not given" (or "Distributor not given"). The legacy labelled the column with the dash (07_engine.js:2050), which the house style keeps for a missing value alone in a cell (D-029).

entries.description: The holding whose Crore market value is "12abc" has an invalid market value and is excluded and listed; its Lakh value is not used in its place (KI-147, the owner's answer of 24 Oct 2026: no fallback). The legacy parseFloat read 12 Crore off the text, which inflated the total, every percentage, the Equity rows and the columns of its client and distributor, and changed the order of the Equity products and of the distributor columns. The placeholder, blank and disagreeing rows of the file read the same in both.

The holding whose Crore invested value is "12abc" has an invalid invested value and counts as one without an invested value; its Lakh value is not used in its place (KI-147). The holding excluded for its market value (AG-13) takes its invested value out of the totals. The legacy read 12 Crore of invested value off the text and summed both.
